question: What do the energy theories of money and value (Soddy, Technocracy, Odum, Hall, Ayres, Keen, Garrett) establish, and what numbers do they carry?

findings.finding: Wealth is energy work that empowers life; money, credit and legal claims are debts, not wealth, and real wealth is subject to conservation laws while debt is not.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Money, credit, and other legal claims to wealth are debts, rather than wealth. Labour and inventions are not wealth, though essential factors in its production. The physical definition of wealth is a form or product of energy or work which enables or empowers life.

findings.finding: Interest is legitimate as hire of organs of production making perishable wealth; extending perennial interest to the non-repayment of any debt is the failure of the capitalistic era; capital multiplies efficiency of human time but not time itself.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The failure of the capitalistic era is due to the nature of interest and ‘capital’ being misunderstood, and to the idea of perennial interest being extended from payment for the use of organs of production in the production of perishable wealth to payment for the non-repayment of any sort of debt.

findings.finding: Virtual wealth: a community acts as if it held wealth equal to the purchasing power of its money; the money quantity is arbitrary and the value of money is measured by virtual wealth; Soddy proposes a currency based on an index number.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: It is the virtual wealth which measures the value or purchasing power of money, and not money which measures the value of wealth.

sources.population: theory of money, wealth and debt (Nobel chemist, scan titled 1925 on archive.org)
notFound: No energy-denominated unit of account is proposed in the passages read; the proposal is an index-number currency.

item.title: What is the minimum EROI that a sustainable society must have?

findings.finding: Minimum EROI at the mine-mouth or farm-gate is about 3:1 for oil and for corn ethanol; below it a fuel needs subsidy from other energy.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: we calculate for both oil and corn-based ethanol as about 3:1 at the mine-mouth/farm-gate. Since most biofuels have EROI’s of less than 3:1 they must be subsidized by fossil fuels to be useful.

notFound: Society-level minimum EROI figures beyond the mine-mouth value are in the body text, which the publisher site did not serve.

item.title: Energy, EROI and quality of life

findings.finding: Energy indices correlate with higher standard of living, with a saturation point above 150 GJ per capita or above EROI 20:1.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: We also find a saturation point at which increases in per capita energy availability (greater than 150 GJ) or EROI (above 20:1) are not associated with further improvement to society.

sources.population: national energy indices against quality-of-life indicators (HDI, child underweight, health expenditure, gender inequality index, literacy, improved water)
notFound: Number of countries and regression coefficients are in the body text, paywalled.

item.title: Past world economic production constrains current energy demands: persistent scaling with implications for economic growth and climate change mitigation

findings.finding: Current world primary energy consumption stays at a constant ratio to the time integral of past real production: 5.9 plus or minus 0.1 gigawatts per trillion 2010 US dollars (2 percent standard deviation; 5.2 or 6.2 if the starting cumulative production is doubled or halved).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: the ratio of the two remained nearly unchanged, that is λ = E(t)/W(t) = 5.9 ± 0.1 Gigawatts per trillion 2010 US dollars.

findings.finding: Holding no further efficiency gains, stabilising emissions needs at least one gigawatt of renewable or nuclear capacity per day, or a steady-state economy devoting production to metabolic needs.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: options look limited to rapid decarbonization of energy consumption through sustained implementation of at least one Gigawatt of renewable or nuclear power capacity per day

sources.population: world primary energy consumption and inflation-adjusted world production, 1980 to 2017

item.title: Modelling energy transition risk: the impact of declining energy return on investment (EROI)

findings.finding: Simulated transitions with falling EROI give an initial output rise followed by recession, stagflation, rising inequality and stranded assets, increasing with capital intensity of green energy and EROI decline.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The negative effects associated with the transition – recession, stagnation, stagflation, increasing inequality and asset stranding – are positively related to the capital intensity of green energy production and reductions in EROI.

sources.population: stock-flow-consistent input-output model TranSim with energy, capital and other-goods sectors

item.title: A non-conforming technocratic dream: Howard Scott’s technocracy movement

findings.finding: Technocracy rested on scientific management and Veblen, aimed at maximizing productive efficiency and minimizing waste, and presented an ecological vision in the idea of energy certificates; its productivist premise and political disorganization led to failure.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: the technocracy presented, if accidentally, an ecological vision manifest in the idea of energy certificates.

notFound: Denomination, issuance and accounting rules of the energy certificate come from Technocracy primary texts, which were not read.
